items.stem: What should you do with an explanation Codex gives about unfamiliar code?

options.text: Check it against the actual code before relying on it
options.rationale: Correct: verify explanations against the source.

options.text: Ignore the code and trust the summary only
options.rationale: The code is the source of truth, not the summary.

items.stem: Why plan a feature file-by-file before letting Codex implement it?

options.text: It clarifies the affected surface and the tests that must change
options.rationale: Correct: a plan maps scope and the tests involved.
Planning does not reduce repo size.

options.text: It removes the need to read any diffs
options.rationale: Diffs must still be read after implementation.
Planning reduces risk but does not guarantee bug-free code.

items.stem: Which TWO practices keep Codex-assisted development safe in a real codebase? (Select TWO)

options.text: Read every diff before accepting it
options.rationale: Correct: reviewing diffs catches unwanted changes.

options.text: Keep changes on a branch under review and version control
options.rationale: Correct: branches and review contain risk.

options.text: Let the agent edit and merge with no review
Skip running the tests to save time
options.rationale: Tests verify the change and should be run.

items.explanation: Correct: reviewing diffs catches unwanted changes.
